gloss: to close up completely; to shut tight

definitions.gloss: to close up completely; to keep shut
definitions.explanation: To close doors, windows, or curtains completely and leave them that way, often for an extended period. Implies sealing a space off from the outside.

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}を{閉|し}め{切|き}って{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: I closed all the windows tight and went out.

examples.japanese: カーテンを{閉|し}め{切|き}ったままだと、{部屋|へや}が{暗|くら}くて{気分|きぶん}が{沈|しず}む。
examples.english: Keeping the curtains shut all the time makes the room dark and lowers my mood.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}の{間|あいだ}、{使|つか}っていない{部屋|へや}は{閉|し}め{切|き}っておくと{暖房|だんぼう}{費|ひ}が{節約|せつやく}できる。
examples.english: Keeping unused rooms closed up during winter helps save on heating costs.

notes:
Compound of {閉|し}める (to close) + {切|き}る (to do thoroughly). The 〜きる suffix here signals completeness — not just closing, but closing entirely and keeping closed.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive (takes を).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {窓|まど}を{閉|し}め{切|き}る: to keep the windows closed
- カーテンを{閉|し}め{切|き}る: to keep the curtains closed
- ドアを{閉|し}め{切|き}る: to keep the door closed
- {部屋|へや}を{閉|し}め{切|き}る: to seal off a room

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {閉|し}める: to close — neutral, just the action of closing
- {締|し}め{切|き}る (05743): to set a deadline; to close registration — homophone, different kanji and meaning
- {閉|と}じる: to close (a book, eyes) — used for things that fold or come together
